nodes.summary: KNAPSACK is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to a knapsack instance $(I, C, T)$ for which some subsequence of the item list $I$, possibly empty, has total weight at most $C$ and total value at least $T$. Bitstrings that do not decode are rejected.
nodes.title: The KNAPSACK decision problem

nodes.summary: A knapsack instance $(I, C, T)$, with item list $I$, capacity $C$ and target value $T$, is feasible when some subsequence of $I$, possibly empty, has total weight at most $C$ and total value at least $T$. Repeated items in $I$ are distinct occurrences that can be selected separately.
nodes.title: Feasible knapsack instances

nodes.summary: A 0/1 knapsack instance is a triple $(I, C, T)$ of a list $I$ of items, each a pair $(w, v)$ of natural numbers giving its weight $w$ and value $v$, a natural-number capacity $C$, and a natural-number target value $T$.
nodes.title: Knapsack instances

nodes.summary: The KNAPSACK decision problem is in NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.
nodes.title: KNAPSACK is NP-complete

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
